newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal prices ease on low export demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal prices ease on low export demand.

text.p: Indian soymeal prices fell by nearly $13 per tonne in the past fortnight on a lack of export demand as foreign buyers were waiting for prices to fall further before signing contracts, traders said on Tuesday.
"Soymeal (export) prices have decreased by $13 per tonne within 15 days and prices may further decrease," said Prakash Vohra, a leading oilmeal broker.
Traders said soymeal export prices were currently quoted at $265 per tonne FAS compared to $210 last year. Last week it was quoted at around $269 per tonne.
Soybean has risen nearly 500 rupees during the last 10 days to around 10,400-10,700 rupees per tonne compared to around 8,250-8,500 the same time last year due to poor arrivals, traders said.
They said nearly 8,000 tonnes of soybean was currently arriving per day compared to 20,000 tonnes last year in the markets of central India, the hub of India's soybean processing industry.
"Arrivals were just 40 percent compared to last year's arrivals at the same time," said Dinesh Jadhav, a leading oilmeal broker.
Last week, traders said soybean prices firmed in the local markets on poor crop arrivals as farmers held back stocks to sell later at higher prices.
In plant delivery conditions, soybean was quoted at 10,500-10,850 rupees per tonne against 8,350-8,650 rupees during the same time last year.
